# UI/UX Visual Design Guidance

Improve the interface into a premium, trustworthy, modern public-service product.

## Design priorities
- Use a modern SaaS design language with generous spacing and strong hierarchy.
- Keep the app calm, clean, and credible rather than flashy.
- Prioritize accessible readability, clear actions, and high trust.
- Make every screen feel conversion-friendly and polished.

## Visual system
- Use a palette based on deep navy, slate, white, and blue/teal accents.
- Reserve accent colors for primary CTAs, status chips, and highlights.
- Use subtle shadows, soft borders, and consistent radius values.
- Keep the layout balanced and uncluttered.

## Layout and component rules
- Use consistent 8px spacing.
- Prefer card layouts, section grouping, and aligned column structures.
- Create strong hero sections and CTA hierarchy.
- Make dashboards and forms feel structured and low-friction.
- Keep content scannable and easy to read on mobile and desktop.

## UX behavior
- Make the interface feel reassuring and action-oriented.
- Show clear states for loading, success, validation, and empty content.
- Improve flow clarity for login, registration, dashboard, and forms.
- Reduce friction in service discovery and decision-making tasks.

## Content and polish
- Use clear, human, trustworthy language.
- Avoid generic AI-chat styling and overly playful visuals.
- Prefer premium polish, crisp typography, and strong visual rhythm.

## Implementation preferences
- Reuse clean reusable components instead of scattered ad hoc styles.
- Keep CSS organized, maintainable, and responsive.
- Use smooth but subtle hover, focus, and motion states.
- Improve accessibility with visible focus rings and good contrast.
